changed_in.5.2: Reports `true` for bodies that used to fail. A coroutine that suspends from inside a protected call, a metamethod or a generic `for` loop's iterator is refused in 5.1, so the resume that started it comes back `false` with an error object; from here on the same body suspends and the yielded values arrive after the status.
changed_in.5.5: An error object of `nil` is replaced by a string before it propagates, so the second value on the failing path is a string where earlier versions hand back `nil`. A body that calls `error()` with no argument at all is the usual way to reach it. This is also the first version in which a resume can come back because the coroutine closed itself: `coroutine.close()` on the running coroutine does not return there, and this call returns instead, with `true` and no values after it, or `false` and an error object should a closing method raise. Earlier versions refuse that close, so a resume there comes back only when the body suspends, stops or fails.
